newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to fight crime with TV appeals.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to fight crime with TV appeals.

text.p: Belgian crime fighters, spurred on by public outrage over their slowness in catching the men behind a paedophile ring, will take to the television later this month to appeal for help with unresolved cases.
Programme makers said on Tuesday the country's first televised Appeal for Witnesses programmes -- one in Dutch and one in French -- would aim to serve the public and avoid sensationalism.
The idea for the monthly 50-minute shows, which have the backing of the Justice Ministry, was born in November 1995 after four young girls went missing.
It was given added impetus when the girls' bodies were found late last summer, driven by the parents of other missing children and pressure from public opinion.

The girls died in the hands of a gang which police say was led by convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux who has been charged with kidnapping, paedophile sex and rape, murder as well as car theft and trafficking in stolen cars.
Two other girls were rescued from a dungeon in one of Dutroux's houses and the search for other missing children was stepped up amid fears they too had fallen victim to Dutroux and his accomplices.
Parents of the victims have publicly complained about the poor reaction from police, the gendarmerie and investigating magistrates when they first reported their offspring's disappearance.
Public inquiries into police handling of the cases have revealed bungling and inept coordination between various services.

The Dutch programme aimed at Flanders in the north will go out on commercial station VTM on February 24, to be followed three days later by its French-language cousin on RTBF state television for Wallonia in the south.
Viewers will be invited to phone in tip-offs on freephone numbers.
